Theorem
[distance-preserving bijections are isometries]

Source: petersen:page-0219 ↗ def:pet-ch5-distance-coordinates ↗ def:pet-ch5-local-isometry 1. ch5:5.6.15If $F:M\to N$ is a bijection between Riemannian manifolds with $|F(p)F(q)|_{g_N}=|pq|_{g_M}$ for all $p,q\in M$, then $F$ is a Riemannian isometry.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch5-myers-steenrod-isometry \sketch Choose distance coordinates at $q=F(p)$ as in subsection 6.3, with poles $q_i=F(p_i)$. Then $r_{q_i}\circ F(x)=|xp_i|$, which is smooth near $p$; hence $F$ is smooth in these coordinates. For $v\in T_pM$, take the short segment $c(t)=\exp _p(tv)$. Distance preservation gives

\[ |t-s|\cdot |v|=|c(t)c(s)|_{g_M}=|F(c(t))F(c(s))|_{g_N}, \]

Therefore

\[ |DF(v)|=\left|\frac{d(F\circ c)}{dt}\right|_{t=0} =\lim _{t\to 0}\frac{|F(c(t))F(c(0))|_{g_N}}{|t|} =\lim _{t\to 0}\frac{|c(t)c(0)|_{g_M}}{|t|}=|\dot c(0)|=|v|. \]

□
